saints.name: The Seven Holy Brothers
saints.title: Martyrs
saints.shortBlurb: Seven brothers, sons of St. Felicity, who were put to death for Christ at Rome…
biography: Januarius, Felix, Philip, Silvanus, Alexander, Vitalis, and Martial are seven martyrs whom Rome has kept together on 10 July from the fourth century: the Depositio Martyrum, the calendar of Pope Liberius's time, already assigns them to that day, buried in four cemeteries along the Salarian and Appian Ways.

Their sixth-century Acts, which Gregory the Great cites in his homilies, make them the sons of the widow Felicity. Denounced by the pagan priests, mother and sons stood before the prefect Publius and refused to sacrifice; handed to four judges — answering to their four places of burial — they were put to death under Marcus Aurelius, about the year 164.

Januarius, the eldest, was scourged to death; Felix and Philip were beaten with clubs; Silvanus was hurled from a height; the three youngest were beheaded; and their mother, who had strengthened each in turn, crowned their witness with her own. The story of seven brothers upheld by their mother deliberately echoes the Maccabees, and their feast was long kept under the name of the Seven Holy Brothers.
saints.knownFor: Their martyrdom at Rome as sons of St. Felicity.

sources.text: The Roman Martyrology (1914 English ed.; public domain)
